title: Transcriptional profiling of bacterial peptide-stimulated proliferating NK cells
description: Natural killer (NK) cells expressing the activating receptor KIR2DS4 have been proposed to recognize bacteria peptides from conserved recombinase A (RecA) epitopes presented by HLA-C. However, whether this mechanism operates uniformly across donors and which host genetic factors determine the nature and magnitude of the response remained unknown. To address these questions, we characterized KIR2DS4-expressing NK cell responses to bacterial RecA-derived peptides IVDKSGAWL (IVDL, Helicobacter pylori) and IVDKSGAWF (IVDF, Campylobacter jejuni) in donors confirmed to express functional KIR2DS4. Proliferative responses were evaluated by CFSE dilution in autologous system in HLA-C05 donors, and transcriptional programs of peptide-proliferated NK cells were characterized by bulk RNA sequencing. Transcriptional profiling of proliferating NK cells confirmed consistent upregulation of KIR2DS4 alongside canonical effector transcripts including GZMB, IFNG, and IL2RA across donors, and revealed activation of the PI3K signaling pathway shared by IVDF-responsive cells. These findings demonstrate that KIR2DS4+ NK cell responses to bacterial peptides are heterogeneous, genetically structured, and associated with selective expansion of a KIR2DS4-expressing effector NK cell population, suggesting a role for this receptor in shaping donor-specific immune memory against bacterial pathogens.
